task_name: Date fields and project/phase pickers on input surfaces

strengths: The project→phase reset invariant is enforced structurally, not just by convention: the project picker submits `{projectId, phaseId: null}` in one request (TrackerDetailPage.tsx:568-570) and the phase options are derived exclusively from `selectedProject.phases` (TrackerDetailPage.tsx:410-416), so a cross-project pair is unrepresentable from the UI even under a stale-render race

Shared TrackerDateFields is created unconditionally as the packet required, and both surfaces render it — neither inlined its own date markup (TrackerCreateModal.tsx:397-403, TrackerDetailPage.tsx:533-540)

No client-side duplication of the server's date rules: neither surface compares start against end; both send raw YYYY-MM-DD and render the server's 400 inline (TrackerCreateModal.tsx:201-205, TrackerDetailPage.tsx:346-349)

The detail-page save patch only includes startDate/endDate when the draft actually differs from the server baseline (TrackerDetailPage.tsx:312-317), keeping the existing minimal-PATCH shape and not disturbing the version-conflict path

Date drafts were correctly threaded through every existing draft lifecycle hook — applyItem's unsaved-draft preservation (111-116), `dirty` (281-286), discardDraft (360-368) — rather than bolted on beside them
No new picker was built; both rail selectors reuse TrackerPropertyPicker with its existing prop contract
Scope was respected exactly: the two commits touch only the five files listed in the packet
Verified green: the two target test files pass (27 tests), the full client suite passes (471 tests, 63 files), `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` both clean

issues.description: The inline 400 renders the server's raw string verbatim ('end date must not precede start date' — server/src/routes/tracker-item-parsers.ts:228), which is lowercase and unpunctuated, unlike the surrounding client copy ('Couldn't save the tracker item. Check your connection and try again.'). The QUALITY BAR asks for the brief's neutral-friendly register; the packet also asked for the returned message to be rendered inline, and the server copy is out of T16's scope, so this is noted rather than blocking.
saveError is cleared only on a successful save or Discard, not when the user edits the offending date fields. After a 400 the stale message stays visible while the member corrects the range.

Picker-driven mutations still report any 400 as a connection failure toast. Now that project/phase pickers exist, a stale-data 400 (phase deleted or moved between load and pick) surfaces as 'Check your connection and try again' rather than inline validation, unlike the save path corrected in f6ba459.

The phase picker renders even when the item has no project, showing an empty popover ('No matches') with an onSelect that returns early — a dead affordance. There is also no 'No project' / 'No phase' option, so assignment cannot be cleared from this surface, though unassignment is not part of the DELIVERABLE.

A queued project change is not reflected in phaseOptions until its PATCH resolves, so picking a phase during that window submits the old (still consistent) project/phase pair and silently reverts the project change. The must-not invariant is not violated — the pair is always internally consistent — but the interaction is surprising.

TrackerDetailPage.tsx grew from 460 to 611 lines and handleSave is now ~70 lines. Splitting was not available to the implementer: the packet's must-not-have forbids creating or modifying files outside the listed scope, and the file was already past the size guidance before this task.

`npx biome format` reports drift in TrackerDetailPage.tsx (lines 80-82, 249-256, 404) and TrackerDetailPage.test.tsx (line 563). This matches the repo baseline — 19 other client/server files drift the same way and the pre-commit hook runs only lint + typecheck, not format — so it is a convention gap rather than a T16 regression.
Rail inputs carry both a wrapping
